title: A finite free algebra with field closed fibre over a DVR
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra that is free of finite positive rank as an $A$-module, meaning that it has an $A$-module basis indexed by a finite nonempty set [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Suppose $B/\pi B$ is a nonzero field, where $\pi B$ is the ideal generated by the image of $\pi$. Then $A\to B$ is injective, $B$ is a discrete valuation ring, and its maximal ideal is $\pi B$. No domain, localness, completeness or separability hypothesis on $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, proof, p-base preparation paragraph: the assertion that the finite root algebras are weakly unramified extensions of discrete valuation rings

proof.text: Write $f:A\to B$, $t=f(\pi)$ and fix a finite nonempty basis $(e_i)$. Basis coordinates show that multiplication by any nonzero $a\in A$ is injective on $B$, since $A$ is a domain. If $f(a)=0$ with $a\ne0$, then $ae_i=0$ for every $i$, contradicting that a basis vector is nonzero. Thus $f$ is injective, $t\ne0$, and multiplication by every $t^n$ is injective. The finite basis also makes $B$ a finitely generated $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, unit-times-uniformizer-power assertion and principal-ideal argument; agent-written finite-basis extension of the argument for the finite-stage assertion in Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], $B$ is integral over $A$. For any maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal] gives $f^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$, since $A$ is local. Hence $tB\subseteq\mathfrak n$. The field hypothesis makes $tB$ maximal: if an ideal strictly contains it, any element with nonzero class has an inverse modulo $tB$, so that ideal contains $1$. Thus every maximal ideal equals $tB$, and this is the unique maximal ideal of $B$.

e0}n_i$ and divide all coordinates by $\pi^n$, obtaining $x=t^ny$. At least one coordinate of $y$ is a unit of $A$, so $y
otin tB$: membership in $tB$ would make every coordinate divisible by $\pi$, and a unit cannot belong to the proper ideal $\pi A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion] in the local ring from Step 2, $y$ is a unit of $B$. Every nonzero $x$ therefore has the form $t^ny$ with $y$ a unit.

proof.text: For nonzero $x=t^nu$ and $z=t^mv$ as in Step 3, $xz=t^{n+m}uv\ne0$: multiplication by $t^{n+m}$ is injective by Step 1, while $uv$ is a unit and $1\ne0$ because $B/tB$ is a nonzero field. Thus $B$ is an integral domain.

proof.text: The zero ideal is principal. For any nonzero ideal $I$ of $B$, choose $0\ne x=t^nu\in I$ with exponent $n$ least among the exponents of all its nonzero elements in Step 3; such a least exponent exists in $\mathbf N$. Then $t^n=xu^{-1}\in I$. For $0\ne z=t^mv\in I$ minimality gives $m\ge n$, and $z=t^n(t^{m-n}v)$, so $I=t^nB$. Thus every ideal is principal. Step 2 gives localness and maximal ideal $tB$; this ideal is nonzero by Step 1 and proper by the field quotient. Together with Step 4, these are precisely the DVR conditions in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

Statement: A is a DVR with uniformizer π, B is a commutative A-algebra with a finite nonempty basis, and B/πB is a nonzero field; then A→B is injective and B is a DVR with maximal ideal πB. Checked against Stacks Tag 00PD (algebra.tex l.29104, the u·π^n factorization) and Tag 09II (more-algebra.tex l.35961, the p-base paragraph on weakly unramified finite extensions of DVRs). Step 1 (elementary): basis coordinates give injectivity, t^n is a nonzerodivisor, B is finite. Step 2: finite gives integral (lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral), and a maximal ideal contracts to a maximal one (lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal), so the contraction is m_A=πA; tB is maximal because the quotient is a field; so B is local with maximal ideal tB. Step 3: a PID is Noetherian, so lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power applies to A coordinatewise; with the minimal exponent, y has a unit coordinate, so y is not in tB and is a unit by lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion. Steps 4-5 (elementary): B is a domain, every ideal is t^nB, and tB is nonzero and proper, which are all clauses of def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring. Small cases: Z_(p)[i] with p≡3 mod 4 is consistent; p≡1 mod 4 and A[t]/(t^2-π) are excluded by the field hypothesis. Every cited node is a Mathlib-leaf or definition node whose statement says what the step uses. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no tool_uses are needed. A duplicate search with rg -L found no other node stating this criterion. The blueprint record matches the parent lem-sfb-dvr-perfect-residue-algebraic-tower, whose Step 3 uses exactly this statement. No changes.
